# What we got wrong about screed drying times

Last January we laid a cement screed in an old house in Bath. After three weeks the CM meter still read 2.8%. Our flooring supplier's guidance says parquet needs 2.0% or less ([guidance note](https://example.org/guide)), so we had to wait.

The reason was mundane. The windows were sealed, the heating ran at half power and the owner wanted to save energy. We set up two dehumidifiers and aired the rooms every morning. Ten days later the reading was 1.9.

I mention this because we get the question almost every week. How long does screed need to dry? The rule of thumb, one week per centimetre, only holds in good weather. At 6 cm thick and 12 °C you can easily plan for twice that.

In our regression we used robust standard errors, and the leverage of a few outliers was small. The test harness ran every night.

What actually helps? Three things:

1. Cross-ventilate twice a day, don't tilt the windows.
2. Heat to at least 18 °C once the manufacturer allows it.
3. Measure, don't guess. A CM test costs us £40 and saves a ruined floor.

If you are unsure, call us. We come round and measure before the floor goes down.
